voice.name: Emma
voice.processing: Fixed gain and scheduled silence; no time stretching or pitch change

presentation: Readable walkthrough of real saved CLI outputs; source text and numeric outputs unchanged. Every CLI invocation is a separate process.

beats.title: Keep the lesson for the next run
beats.text: A new agent session should not mean explaining the same project instruction again. Here is one lesson from our Harbour project brief.

beats.title: Save the actual instruction
beats.text: I save the validation instruction as memory, with a tag identifying its source. The saved item contains the exact lesson, not just a label saying something was captured.

beats.title: Read it back in another process
beats.text: That command has finished. A new process opens the saved item by its identifier. The same instruction is still there, ready to inspect or export.

beats.title: Connect the words to the project
beats.text: The project role has a small knowledge graph. Validate brief, brief validation, and the check option name the same concept. The note also names the project brief.

beats.title: Find the lesson by its meaning
beats.text: I search for validate brief. The graph retrieves the saved instruction and its source tag. This is the actual stored text, rather than a newly generated answer.

beats.title: Check when it should stay quiet
beats.text: An unrelated question returns no memory. So does the finance role, and a separate empty store. Roles shape retrieval; separate folders hold separate stores.

beats.title: Try it on a clean example
beats.text: Download the public brief, graph, commands and saved results. Next, we will use the same project to show a failed command, a reviewed correction, and what an agent actually executes.
